Look up nicknames, formal names and a canonical form for first names

Source: R/nicknames.R
nickname_lookup.Rd

Matches each first name exactly (after upper-casing) against the bundled first_name_pairs table. Returns the name's formal forms, its nicknames, and one canonical form for grouping. A name can be both a nickname and a formal name (KATIE: a nickname of KATHERINE and the formal form of KATE). Only direct pairs are listed: two nicknames of one name (BETH, LISA) are not each other's variants.

Usage

nickname_lookup(
  first_name,
  gender = NULL,
  gender_confidence = NULL,
  salutation = NULL,
  sep = ";; ",
  min_confidence = 80,
  min_share = 0.6,
  min_nick_rate = 0.002,
  spelling = c("lexicon", "misspelling")
)

Arguments

first_name

Character vector of first names.

gender

Optional vector of "M", "F" or "U", as returned by parse_name(), used to choose among formal names.

gender_confidence

Optional vector of gender confidence (0-100), as returned by parse_name().

salutation

Optional vector of salutations, as returned by parse_name(); MR, MRS, MS and MISS set the gender.

sep

Separator for the list columns. Defaults to ";; ".

min_confidence

Minimum gender_confidence (0-100) to trust census gender. Defaults to 80.

min_share

Share of the nickname evidence the top formal name needs. Defaults to 0.6.

min_nick_rate

Minimum ratio of people carrying the name as a nickname (people with the name and a formal form) to national records with the name, for the name to be resolved. Defaults to 0.002.

spelling

Which spelling pairs define spelling roots: any of "lexicon" (reviewed spelling pairs), "misspelling" (rare forms of common names), "sound_alike" (unreviewed sound-alike pairs). Defaults to c("lexicon", "misspelling").

Value

A data.frame with one row per input and columns first_name_type (formal, nickname, both, variant for a name only in spelling, cognate or compound pairs, unknown, initial, or "" for a missing name), first_name_formal, first_name_nicknames, first_name_canonical, and canonical_rule (self, spelling, nickname, ambiguous).

Details

Canonical rule.

  1. Spelling root. Each name moves to its most common spelling variant, repeatedly, while that is more common nationally (KATHRYN -> KATHERINE -> CATHERINE; STEVEN -> STEPHEN). Spelling pairs come from the reviewed lexicon and, by default, the misspelling rows (a rare form of a common name, used only when the rare form has fewer than 1,000 national records: MARCO is not a misspelling of MARK).

  2. Nickname step. A name whose spelling family is mostly carried as a nickname, by at least min_nick_rate of the people with that name (so MARK, a name in its own right, is not resolved to MARCUS), is resolved to a formal name. Its direct formal partners are grouped by spelling root and weighted by the number of people carrying each pair; partners that are themselves nicknames are dropped when others exist; with known gender, partners of the other gender are dropped. The top group wins with at least min_share of the weight. Otherwise the name is "ambiguous" and keeps its spelling root (KATHY: KATHLEEN vs KATHERINE; AL: ALAN vs ALBERT; PAT with no gender).

  3. Chains are not followed: one nickname step at most, so KATHLEEN and CATHERINE are not merged through KATE.

Gender comes from a gendered salutation (MR, MRS, MS, MISS), otherwise from gender when gender_confidence >= min_confidence.

Examples

nickname_lookup(c("BOB", "KATHY", "KATIE", "PAT", "PAT", "STEVEN", "KAREN", "J"),
                gender = c("M", "F", "F", "F", "U", "M", "F", "U"),
                gender_confidence = c(99, 99, 99, 90, 50, 99, 99, 50))
#>   first_name_type                                   first_name_formal
#> 1            both                                              ROBERT
#> 2        nickname          KATHLEEN;; KATHRYN;; KATHERINE;; KATHARINE
#> 3        nickname KATHERINE;; KATE;; KATHLEEN;; CATHERINE;; KATHARINE
#> 4            both                                    PATRICIA;; PATSY
#> 5            both                          PATRICIA;; PATRICK;; PATSY
#> 6          formal                                                    
#> 7         variant                                                    
#> 8         initial                                                    
#>   first_name_nicknames first_name_canonical canonical_rule
#> 1          BOBBY;; ROB               ROBERT       nickname
#> 2                                     KATHY      ambiguous
#> 3                                 CATHERINE       nickname
#> 4                PATTY             PATRICIA       nickname
#> 5                PATTY                  PAT      ambiguous
#> 6                STEVE              STEPHEN       spelling
#> 7                                     KAREN           self
#> 8                                         J           self
